PullRequest.Title: Show an error when a new skill's name already exists
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #348809

**Problem:** Choosing **New Skill** with the name of an existing skill closed the name prompt and did nothing: `createFile` threw on the existing `SKILL.md` and the command rejected silently.

**Change:**
- The name prompt now validates that `<name>/SKILL.md` doesn't exist ("A skill with this name already exists").
- An existing folder without a `SKILL.md` is still accepted, and the skill file is added to it, as before.
- A name taken by a file (not a folder) is rejected with "A file with this name already exists".
- If creating the folder or file still fails, for example because `SKILL.md` appeared after validation, an error notification is shown instead of a silent failure.

**Tests:**
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` and `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/newPromptFileActions.test.ts`: 6 passing. The two new cases fail without the change.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on both changed files: clean.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- UI scenario (Customizations > Skills > New Skill with an existing name) on a dev build: the prompt stays open and shows the error, and `SKILL.md` is unchanged.

## Before / after

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing and accepting a skill name in a local or remote workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The input remains interactive during asynchronous validation. Acceptance waits for the current validation promise: one stat for an existing SKILL.md, otherwise two sequential stats. Previously validation performed only bounded string checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the proposed SKILL.md and, if it does not exist, stat its parent to detect a conflicting plain file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider/channel stat for a detected existing skill; two sequential provider/channel stats for an available name, an empty skill folder, or a conflicting plain file. At most 2K calls over K validated values; no directory enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Zero filesystem metadata or IPC calls during skill-name validation; creation checks happened after acceptance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The unfinished portion of current validation delays accepting the name. Other validation runs can overlap; they do not synchronously block typing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For vscode-remote targets, send those stat requests through the existing remoteFilesystem channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same one or two metadata requests per validated candidate, not additional per-skill or per-folder fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This remote channel was used by creation, but not by skill-name validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote round-trip latency contributes to the pending validation awaited on acceptance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform symlink-aware metadata lookup using lstat and a fallback stat when needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Ordinarily one filesystem lookup per existing non-symlink path and two per missing path. An entirely missing candidate produces four underlying lookups across the two provider stats; symlinks and platform-specific fallback can add lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No corresponding lookups while validating the skill name.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These asynchronous lookups must finish for their metadata request to resolve.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K syntactically valid, changed input values actually delivered after the 100 ms debounce; not the number of skills or workspace folders. Invalid or empty names issue zero file calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: QuickInput debounces value-change validation by 100 ms and checks value equality. Each candidate's two requests are sequential. Different candidates may overlap when providers are slow; there is no new collection-wide fan-out or global limiter on this validation path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application-level positive or negative metadata cache. QuickInput reuses the latest validation promise when the raw value is unchanged, including acceptance; revisiting an earlier value can validate again. OS metadata caches may reduce local cost without removing calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the callback through QuickInput's debounce and acceptance logic to provider stat, local IPC, remote channel, and filesystem lookup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and remote latency are unmeasured. Overlap depends on typing cadence and latency; there is no demonstrated heavyweight operation beyond individual metadata checks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable high-confidence regression. The added bounded metadata checks implement the requested live validation, use existing input coalescing, and match the adjacent prompt-name validation pattern. Extra round trips alone do not establish an actionable scaling bug.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selecting the destination through the New Skill command without a supplied target folder
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Source-folder resolution and the user's folder selection precede the name prompt. The changed validation is invoked only after one destination has been selected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve user home from the remote environment through the existing path service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Await the path service's stored user-home promise; not one environment fetch per configured location or validation callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical path-service resolution before showing the folder picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Folder resolution waits for this promise on a cold environment; warm calls reuse it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: When parent-repository customizations are enabled, stat ancestor .git entries until a repository root or stopping boundary is reached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider stat per visited ancestor, serial within the traversal and across workspace roots, with a ResourceSet stopping already-covered paths. Disabled parent lookup does not perform this traversal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same traversal, stopping conditions, and call count existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The optional traversal finishes before destination choices are presented; local IPC or remote network transports follow the selected provider.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace roots and configured source locations, deduplicated by URI. Optional parent-repository lookup additionally depends on ancestor depth, not the count of skill files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parent walks and workspace-root iteration are sequential. Configuration processing does not invoke the new validator per source folder.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: User-home resolution is promise-backed. Source locations are deduplicated; parent stat results are not newly cached or invalidated by this change. A supplied targetFolder bypasses the picker entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced NewSkillFileAction.run through askForPromptSourceFolder, prompts service, source-folder locator, and path service.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace-root count, ancestor depth, and provider latency vary, but all collection-scaling boundary work here is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression: the diff neither repeats destination discovery nor moves it onto another critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating an available skill or adding SKILL.md to an existing folder, then opening its editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After validation, createFolder completes before createFile; file creation completes before the normal or custom opener and snippet insertion. The Customizations editor awaits the same command and then refreshes its list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively ensure the destination folder, resolve its metadata, validate SKILL.md creation, and write its template.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One createFolder and one createFile per accepted action. mkdirp stats missing ancestors and creates them as necessary. Existing createFolder resolution enumerates the destination and resolves immediate-child metadata; createFile retains its existing existence check, write validation, and final file stat. All these counts are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same createFolder/createFile operations and awaits ran before the diff, including existing directory-child metadata fan-out. The diff wraps them in error handling but does not add another creation attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Folder operations and the single file write are serialized before opening; provider calls use existing local IPC or remote filesystem transport.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Convert the fixed skill snippet to insertion text and a VSBuffer, then transmit its bytes to the existing filesystem write path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded template buffer per attempted file creation; no collection copy or file-content read introduced by validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snippet conversion and buffer creation occurred once per creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Template conversion precedes the existing write. The small template string now precedes createFolder, but introduces no heavyweight eager initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the created file's text model for the embedded editor, using the existing text-file read path when needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One canonical-URI model-reference acquisition for the custom opener; a cold file model reads the single small SKILL.md, while an existing reference is shared. The normal opener also receives the same single URI as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same opener, model resolution, and snippet application followed successful creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Editor presentation waits for model resolution after creation, unchanged by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One skill file and a fixed template with a name of at most 64 characters. Existing-folder child count can affect the pre-existing createFolder metadata resolution; missing-ancestor depth affects pre-existing mkdirp.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Folder creation, file creation, and opening remain sequential. Existing destination-child metadata resolution uses settled parallel child work; this is not amplified by the new stat, which explicitly does not resolve children.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Validation results are not reused as authoritative creation metadata, preserving race-safe file creation. Existing text-model references are shared by canonical URI; text-file reads retain their existing etag behavior. No cache ownership changes were introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected file-service creation, directory resolution, buffer/write handling, custom opener, and model-reference acquisition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Destination size and remote latency can make the unchanged creation path expensive; the added validation cost is accounted for separately.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing collection-scaling directory resolution and editor loading are neither increased nor duplicated by the changed lines.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rejecting a conflicting skill name, cancelling the prompt, or reporting a creation race/failure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A known conflict leaves the name prompt open after its metadata validation. Cancellation resolves the prompt without creating or opening anything. If creation subsequently fails, the new catch displays one notification and returns without opening an editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check conflicting metadata and, only after acceptance, execute the existing folder/file creation operations that may fail.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A known existing skill needs one validation stat and no creation calls. A plain-file conflict needs two validation stats and no creation calls. A post-validation race keeps the same single creation attempt and its existing failure checks; no automatic retry follows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Conflicts were not checked in the input; accepting the name attempted creation and rejected on failure. The underlying creation operations were already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Conflict validation is awaited as described above; failure notification follows the failed operation. Cancellation does not await outstanding validation work before resolving the input.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One currently validated name and at most one failed creation attempt per accepted command; no retry loop or retained history is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serial creation attempt per accepted command. Pending validations can overlap as in the typing scenario, but error handling schedules no retries or additional provider work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Known collisions are not pinned in a cache. Outstanding validation promises can finish after cancellation, but QuickInput disposes its input listeners; no new long-lived cache, resource handle, or collection is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed tests corroborate conflict validation and unchanged file contents; changed catch returns before either opener. Static code shows no repeated error-processing loop or new retained state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual provider failures can be slow, but their latency is pre-existing. Notification duration and error-message size are unmeasured, with no evidence of a large or accumulating payload.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix. The new failure notification fixes correctness/feedback, while conflict rejection can avoid unsuccessful creation work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the entire two-file inventory and all diff pages. Traced input scheduling, provider boundaries, destination discovery, creation, editor loading, and failure lifecycle. No high-confidence actionable performance regressions found; no concrete performance fix qualified for blame-based learning. Static read-only review; runtime/provider timings were not measured. The performance guide tool returned an oversized preview; the learned-regression document and supplied full skill instructions were available.
